answer: Ana leads the pricing page redesign. Marco made that explicit in the Q4 planning meeting on 1 September: "the pricing page redesign ships in Q4, Ana leads it, and the target is end of September." [[M1#7]] Ana produced the mockups (three tiers, annual billing toggle, comparison table below the fold) and owns the build [[M1#3]][[M1#5]], and she has continued to run the workstream — reporting the legal delay [[M2#1]], booking Priya for the design review [[M2#28]][[M2#30]], and taking the action items from that review (updated mockups by Thursday) [[M3#12]].

Northwind's invoices exported with the wrong tax rate for their Dutch entity, and their finance team only caught it after some had already been sent to clients — they emailed Marco about it Sunday night [[M1#16]]. Diego traced the cause to the rounding change from August, which only affects accounts with multiple tax jurisdictions — essentially just Northwind [[M1#17]]. Forty-one invoices over two weeks were affected [[M1#19]]. Diego fixed the calculation that day and sent a note with the list of affected invoice numbers by the next morning so Northwind could issue corrections, while Marco called their CFO himself [[M1#20]][[M1#21]]. Regenerating the PDFs was the awkward part since they'd already been sent [[M1#19]].

By the September 15 sync the issue was closed: corrected invoices went out, Northwind's finance team confirmed the numbers, and the CFO replied to Marco's note [[M2#9]]. Marco decided on a credit of one month free, which he'd already told the CFO, and Ana applied it that day [[M2#10]][[M2#11]].

No. In the Q4 planning meeting on September 1, Marco decided outright: "no mobile app in Q4," with a revisit in January if the mobile share changes [[M1#25]]. The reasoning was that only about eight percent of sessions are on a phone, and most of those are people checking invoice status, which the responsive site already handles [[M1#23]], plus it would consume the whole quarter for two people [[M1#24]]. Sofía said she would add a note to the support macro so the team stops promising it [[M1#26]].

That decision held through the September 29 retro, where Marco said the mobile app was cut on purpose and he had "zero regrets," growing more confident each time support asks because the requesters want a feature the responsive site already has [[M2#23]].

One caveat on the record: an AI note-taker trial produced a summary claiming the team had decided to build the mobile app, which Sofía flagged as the opposite of the actual decision; the trial was cancelled as a result [[M3#19]][[M3#23]].

You chose **Drata** at the September 29 retro [[M1#19]].

The three quotes were Vanta, Drata, and Secureframe, all within twenty percent of each other on price [[M1#16]]. Drata had the best Postgres and GitHub integrations, which cover most of your evidence collection; Vanta had a nicer dashboard, and Secureframe was cheapest but had a smaller auditor network [[M1#16]]. Diego argued integrations matter more than the dashboard since he's the one feeding the platform, and Sofía agreed on Drata [[M1#17]][[M1#18]].

Follow-on plan: Marco signs in the first week of October, and Diego kicks off the integrations after the checkout change ships, so late October [[M1#19]]. The audit itself is Q1, since evidence collection takes three months minimum, and Marco said he'd give Northwind that timeline that week [[M1#22]].

The annual discount is **fifteen percent**, down from the twenty percent originally shown. [[M1#6]][[M1#11]] Marco said finance asked for the change as of Friday, explaining that the original twenty percent was a number he made up two years ago and it costs more than it brings in. [[M1#6]][[M1#8]] He took the decision himself: "the number is fifteen. That's a decision, I'll take the complaints." [[M1#11]]

On presentation, Priya argued the saving should be shown in currency rather than only percent — "Save 96 dollars a year" lands harder than "15 percent" — and the team settled on both: percent on the toggle, the amount under each price. [[M1#9]][[M1#10]][[M1#11]] Ana agreed to update the mockups with the new discount by Thursday. [[M1#12]]

The drop-off is at the **billing address step**. Initially Sofía only knew that about a third of people were lost between picking a plan and confirming payment, without knowing which step [[M1#10]], and Diego guessed it was the address form, since a full billing address is requested even for card payments and Stripe doesn't need it [[M1#11]].

Once Diego shipped the funnel events [[M2#10]], the data confirmed his guess: 28% of people who pick a plan leave on the billing address screen [[M2#11]]. After two more weeks of data, Sofía reported the figure as a 29% drop at the billing address step, flat across plans and countries [[M3#1]].

Her recommendation, which Marco approved, is to remove the address step for card payments (Stripe validates the postcode itself) and keep it for bank transfer and invoice-based plans [[M3#1]][[M3#6]].

Marco took the action to get two or three quotes and bring them to the end-of-month retro [[M1#20]], narrowed to Vanta and Drata on Ana's suggestion [[M1#21]][[M1#22]].

Marco stated the Q4 order as: pricing first, then checkout, then SOC 2 groundwork — "in that order, and nothing gets added unless something gets removed." [[M1#25]] He also ruled out the mobile app, saying January at the earliest despite repeated support requests. [[M1#25]]

The reason the order matters, in his words, is that each piece of work changes the numbers the next one depends on: if checkout changes launch in the same week as pricing, "we won't know which one moved conversion, and we'll spend November arguing about it instead of shipping." His rule is one thing at a time, measured, then the next. [[M1#25]] He added that if anyone hears a different version from him, they should tell him, because it means he was wrong in that conversation. [[M1#25]]

This matched what the team had already agreed in Q4 planning, where Sofía said she'd rather launch pricing before starting checkout work, "otherwise I can't tell which change moved the numbers," and Marco agreed.
